note: Generated by xtask/scripts/capture_wizard_guides.py; never edit by hand. `guide_platforms` is GUIDE_PLATFORMS order (the order the checklist and the markdown export iterate), not alphabetical.

youtube.title: YouTube Shorts
youtube.why: Publishes your videos as YouTube Shorts.
steps: Create (or select) a Google Cloud project: https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate (pick an existing project: https://console.cloud.google.com/projectselector2/YOUR_PROJECT_ID)
Open the OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform → Audience): https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/audience

IMPORTANT — click 'Publish App' to move the app to 'In production'. Apps left in 'Testing' issue refresh tokens that EXPIRE AFTER 7 DAYS, so you would have to re-authorize xPST every week. Note: the xPST project's own Google Cloud app is already published to production, so its tokens are long-lived — if you create your own project, publish it to production too (see docs/youtube-oauth-production.md).

Create the OAuth client (Google Auth Platform → Clients → 'Create Client'): https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients (legacy UI: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials → 'Create Credentials' → 'OAuth client ID')

Application type: 'Desktop app'. Name it e.g. 'xPST Desktop'. YouTube scopes are sensitive, so Google may show an 'unverified app' warning during consent — choose 'Advanced' → 'Continue' (fine for personal, single-user use).
Download the client JSON and save it as ~/.xpst/credentials/youtube_client_secrets.json
Back in xPST, re-run `xpst connect youtube` — your browser opens for the one-time Google approval. Sign in and click 'Allow'.

instagram.title: Instagram Reels
instagram.why: Cross-posts your videos as Instagram Reels.
steps: Instagram posting uses the official Meta Graph API. You need a Meta developer app: open https://developers.facebook.com/apps
Click 'Create App' → type 'Business'.
Add the 'Instagram Graph API' product to the app.
Connect your Instagram Business account to a Facebook Page (required by Meta). In Instagram: Settings → Business tools.
Generate a long-lived access token (Graph API Explorer → generate token with instagram_basic + instagram_content_publish permissions, then exchange for a long-lived token).
Paste the token when the wizard asks. It also needs your numeric IG user ID (it can look this up automatically).

x.title: X / Twitter
steps: Option A (official API): open https://developer.x.com and create a Project + App. Free tier allows ~17 posts/day.
Generate the Bearer Token and paste it into the wizard — it verifies immediately against the X API.
Option B (cookies): log into x.com in your browser, export cookies (auth_token + ct0), and choose the cookies option in the wizard.

tiktok.title: TikTok
tiktok.why: Watches a TikTok account as the video source.
steps: For SOURCE mode (watching an account), you only need yt-dlp installed — no app required. The wizard checks this for you (`uv tool install yt-dlp` if missing).
For UPLOADING to TikTok (Content Posting API): open https://developers.tiktok.com/apps and click 'Manage apps' → 'Create app'.
Add the 'Content Posting API' product. Set a redirect URI (e.g. http://localhost:8080/callback). Note the client key and client secret.
Submit the app for audit; while pending you can still post to private/self-only audience from the same account.

threads.title: Threads
threads.why: Posts to Threads via the official Threads API.
steps: Open https://developers.facebook.com/apps
'Create App' → use case 'Threads API access'.
Connect your Threads profile and generate an access token.
Paste the token and your numeric Threads user ID into the wizard.

facebook.title: Facebook Page
facebook.why: Publishes as a Facebook Page (Pages only — personal profiles have no publishing API).
steps: Facebook publishing is Page-scoped and needs your own Meta app: open https://developers.facebook.com/apps
'Create App' → type 'Business', then add the 'Facebook Login for Business' product.
Grant the app pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement and pages_manage_posts (Standard Access is enough for your own Pages).
In the Graph API Explorer pick that app, select the permissions above and generate a User Access Token.
Run `xpst auth facebook` and paste the token (plus the App ID/Secret so the token is exchanged for a long-lived one).
xPST lists your Pages via GET /me/accounts, verifies the chosen Page token and stores it encrypted. No Page → a clear error, never a personal-profile post.

messenger.title: Messenger (optional)
messenger.why: Optional: reply to viewers via Messenger webhook.
steps: This is optional — press Enter to skip unless you need it.
In your Meta app, add the Messenger product.
Generate a Page Access Token and paste it into the wizard.

bluesky.title: Bluesky
bluesky.why: Posts text, images and multi-image posts through the open AT Protocol — no app review, no fee, no developer console.
steps: You need a Bluesky account (any handle, including a custom domain).
Open https://bsky.app/settings/app-passwords
Click 'Add App Password', name it 'xPST' and copy the value.
Run `xpst auth bluesky` and paste your handle and the app password — it is stored encrypted, never in config.yaml.
Video is not supported: Bluesky serves video from a separate service and xPST does not claim it. Text and images publish normally.
